title: Holi: the festival of colors
hook: Prahlad walks out of the fire unharmed; the next morning everyone throws color and nobody is a stranger
tomorrow: Maha Shivaratri: the great night of Shiva

segments.voice: Yesterday: Diwali, a whole city lighting lamps for Rama's return. Light the way home.

A street in north India, on a spring morning. Somebody's uncle is purple. A grandmother is laughing with green powder in her hair. A stranger you've never met walks up, says happy Holi, and smears pink on your cheek, and you do the same back. Water balloons from a balcony. Drums from somewhere. By noon you can't tell the banker from the delivery driver, or the neighbor you haven't spoken to in a year from your own cousin. Everyone is the same muddy, glorious color. But the night before, there was a fire, and the fire is where the story is.
screen: `A STRANGER SMEARS PINK ON YOUR CHEEK.` → `NOBODY CAN TELL WHO IS WHO.` → `BUT FIRST, A FIRE.`

segments.voice: The story is about a boy named Prahlad. His father, Hiranyakashipu, is a demon king with a boon that makes him nearly impossible to kill, and he decides that makes him God. Everyone in the kingdom must worship him. His own son won't. Prahlad keeps saying the name of Vishnu. The Bhagavata Purana tells how the father tries everything to stop him: snakes, elephants, a cliff, poison. The boy survives each one. Then comes the part the festival remembers. The king's sister, Holika, is said to be protected from fire. She takes Prahlad on her lap and sits down in a blazing pyre. And the fire turns. Holika burns. The boy walks out unharmed, still saying the name. An honest note: the Bhagavata tells Prahlad's story at length and ends it with Vishnu appearing as Narasimha, half man and half lion. The Holika scene comes from later tellings and from the festival itself, which is how most people know it. So on the full-moon night of Phalguna, at the end of winter, people light bonfires called Holika Dahan, and many walk around them, remembering a fire that couldn't hold a child. The next morning, the colors. People say it with a grin: bura na mano, Holi hai. Don't be offended, it's Holi. For one day the lines between people get smudged on purpose, and old quarrels are supposed to end. Holi has other stories too, and i'll come back for them. But this one starts with the bonfire.
screen: `A BOY WHO KEEPS SAYING THE NAME.` · `HOLIKA SITS IN THE FIRE.` · `THE BONFIRE THE NIGHT BEFORE.` · `DON'T BE OFFENDED, IT'S HOLI.` · then, large: `EVERYONE'S THE SAME COLOR TODAY.`

segments.voice: Think of someone who annoyed you lately, a small hurt, not a deep wound: a curt message, a friend who forgot. Picture that grudge as a dry stick laid on the bonfire the night before Holi, and watch it burn down to ash. Then picture the morning, and that person standing there with color on their face, the same as yours. You don't have to call them; just notice what feels lighter.
Holi. The spring festival of colors, the morning after the bonfire that remembers Prahlad walking out of the fire.
Your line: everyone's the same color today. For one morning, nobody is a stranger. That's day eighty-two.

howItsDone: Hindus light the Holika Dahan bonfire on the full-moon night of Phalguna and, the next morning, throw colored powder and water with family, neighbors and strangers alike; many use the day to make up after quarrels.

chat.says: Why do people light a big bonfire the night before Holi?
options: To remember Prahlad walking out of Holika's fire unharmed, still saying Vishnu's name.
To burn the winter's leftover colors so new ones can be thrown in the morning.
To remember Holika, who carried her nephew Prahlad safely out of a fire.
chat.meaning: Holika sat in a pyre with Prahlad on her lap. The fire turned: she burned and he walked out. Holika Dahan remembers it.

Prahlad.meaning: the boy who kept saying Vishnu's name despite his father

Hiranyakashipu.meaning: Prahlad's father, a demon king who demanded worship

Holika.meaning: the king's sister, said to be protected from fire

Narasimha.meaning: Vishnu appearing as half man, half lion

Phalguna.meaning: the month at winter's end when Holi falls
